description: deviceId and fingerprint derivation. Fixed X25519 public keys, so both implementations must produce byte-identical identifiers. See ProjectInfo/04-PROTOCOL.md section 2.
algorithm: deviceIdBytes = SHA-256("veyro-id-v1" || staticPublicKey)[0..15];  deviceId = CrockfordBase32(deviceIdBytes);  fingerprint = uppercase hex of deviceIdBytes[0..7], space-separated in pairs

vectors.name: all zero public key
vectors.note: The all-zero public key is not a valid X25519 point, but it is a well-defined byte string and is a useful smoke-test input. This vector exercises the derivation function, not key validity.
vectors.verification: VERIFIED - computed independently of the Kotlin implementation (PowerShell SHA-256 + a separate Crockford encoder) and cross-checked against a Kotlin JVM test. Two independent computations agreeing is the point; a vector copied out of one implementation would only encode that implementation's bugs.

vectors.name: sequential 0x01..0x20 public key
vectors.verification: VERIFIED - same two independent computations as above.

notes: deviceId is 26 Crockford Base32 characters, encoding exactly 16 bytes with no padding.
Crockford Base32 excludes I, L, O and U, and maps I/L to 1 and O to 0 on decode.
The fingerprint bytes come from deviceIdBytes (the first 16 bytes of the digest), not from a re-encoding of the public key.

deviceId MUST be stable across restarts and app updates: the identity seed is persisted, never regenerated. It MUST change when the user resets their identity, because that is genuinely a new key pair.
Domain separation string is exactly "veyro-id-v1" (10 bytes ASCII), prefixed before the 32-byte public key. Getting this wrong changes every deviceId, so it is asserted in its own test.
